facts.text: I was listening to Tchaikovsky's Romeo and Juliet the other day.
I thought the harmony and chords in Romeo and Juliet sounded more modern than Tchaikovsky.
I think both Tchaikovsky and Prokofiev wrote ballet music on love stories, especially fairy tales.
I think Prokofiev's Cinderella shares strange resemblances with Tchaikovsky's Sleeping Beauty.
My music theory isn't good.
I said that Prokofiev's Romeo and Juliet (and not Tchaikovsky's) sounded quite Tchaikvosky.
Tchaikovsky also wrote his own Romeo and Juliet.
I didn't enjoy Tchaikovsky's Romeo and Juliet so much.
I recognize that Tchaikovsky and Prokofiev have different composition styles with similar shared focuses.
I think it was mostly the orchestration and the romantic atmosphere created by the musicality.
Tchaikovsky's art songs don't sound as classical as his ballet music.
I have been listening to a couple of Tchaikovsky's art songs throughout the past couple of days.
I think 'more classical' is a relative definition.
I think Tchaikovsky sounds less classical compared to Beethoven or Bach.
I asked whether Prokofiev was influenced by Tchaikovsky in terms of his interest in ballet music.
I asked about the similarities and differences between Mahler and Shostakovich.
I think musicians influence each other.
I think Stravinsky was heavily influenced by Tchaikovsky and Debussy.
I somewhat hear Stravinsky in Prokofiev.
I can't really hear any traces of Debussy's influence in Prokofiev.
I think both Prokofiev and Tchaikovsky sound modern and romantic.
I think Debussy's music seems more atmospheric.
I think Debussy's music uses more dissonant chords.
I think Debussy's music doesn't place such a heavy emphasis on melody.
I think Debussy seems to be engaged with musical exoticism.
I think Debussy's musical exoticism is somewhat similar to Dvorak.
I am curious about Dvorak in relation to Debussy.
I think Bela Bartok used European folk music.
I think Debussy and Dvorak used music from different cultures that are distant from their own.
I gave examples of foreign music used by Debussy and Dvorak, including Indonesian Gamelan and African American jazz.
I think Bartok's incorporation of Hungarian folk music in his own work is very different.
I asked whether there are composers like Debussy and Dvorak who employed foreign music in their own composition.
I think Bela Bartok was not obviously one of them.
